request.input: Which things should I spend more money on to make life easier Spending extra money on garbage bags with handles has changed my life for the better. Anything other tips like this?

content.text:
We need answer user. Need provide tips on spending more money to make life easier, similar to garbage bags with handles. Need list. We can craft helpful response. Need maybe categories: kitchen, bathroom, travel, tech, clothing, tools. Need emphasize "buy once cry once" etc. Need avoid excessive. Let's think of good examples.

User asks "Which things should I spend more money on to make life easier Spending extra money on garbage bags with handles has changed my life for the better. Anything other tips like this?" Need answer with suggestions. We can include: trash bags with handles already mentioned. Other "upgrade cheap annoyances" items: good kitchen knives, cutting boards? Zip-top bags with slider? Dishwasher pods? Maybe "expensive" but worth it: quality shoes/boots, mattresses, tires, office chair, monitor, keyboard, mouse, headphones, backpack, luggage, rain jacket, winter coat, socks, underwear, bed sheets, towels, toilet paper, paper towels? Actually "spend more money on" items where premium makes big difference.

Need structure: "Things worth upgrading to premium" list with brief why. Maybe 15 items. Need be concise but useful.

Let's brainstorm:

1. Garbage bags with handles (already) - maybe "drawstring trash bags" no rip.

2. Kitchen knives - a good chef's knife ($100+) vs cheap set. Sharpening. Makes cooking easier.

3. Cutting boards - wood or composite, large, non-slip. Doesn't warp.

4. Non-stick pan - but they wear out; maybe cast iron/enameled Dutch oven? Actually spend on good stainless steel/cast iron. But for eggs, cheap nonstick replaced often. Hmm.

5. Dishwasher detergent pods/tabs - quality > powder? Actually pods convenient but expensive; but "Finish Quantum" works better than cheap. Maybe.

6. Laundry detergent - high-efficiency, good stain remover. Or "spend on OxiClean" etc.

7. Toilet paper - 2-ply or better, not thin. Makes life better.

8. Paper towels - select-a-size, strong. Less waste.

9. Tissues with lotion - if colds.

10. Shoes - good walking shoes, work boots, running shoes. Feet support. Also insoles.

11. Mattress and pillows - sleep quality. Pillows: adjustable, good.

12. Bed sheets - high thread count? Actually percale/bamboo? Good sheets.

13. Towels - thick, absorbent, last.

14. Socks - merino wool, cushioned. Darn Tough.

15. Underwear - comfortable, breathable.

16. Office chair - ergonomic, if sit long. Also standing desk.

17. Monitor - large, high-res, USB-C. Less eye strain.

18. Keyboard/mouse - mechanical, ergonomic.

19. Headphones - noise-cancelling, for focus/commute.

20. Phone case/screen protector - protect expensive phone.

21. Power bank - fast charging, high capacity.

22. Cables - braided, long, Anker. Avoid cheap.

23. Luggage - good wheels, warranty.

24. Backpack - comfortable straps, organization.

25. Rain jacket - breathable waterproof.

26. Winter coat - down/insulated.

27. Sunglasses - polarized.

28. Sunscreen - nice texture, not greasy.

29. Skincare - moisturizer, etc.

30. Food storage containers - glass, leak-proof, stackable. Avoid plastic staining.

31. Zip-lock bags - freezer strength, slider.

32. Aluminum foil/parchment paper - heavy duty.

33. Sponges/scrubbers - good ones, replace often.

34. Trash can - foot pedal, easy to clean.

35. Vacuum cleaner - Dyson? Or robot vacuum. Good vacuum makes cleaning easier.

36. Robot vacuum/mop - if budget.

37. Air fryer/instant pot - cooking convenience.

38. Coffee grinder - burr grinder, good beans. Better coffee.

39. Water bottle - insulated, leak-proof.

40. Umbrella - windproof.

Need maybe "spend more on things that separate you from the ground: tires, shoes, mattresses, chairs" classic. Include that.

Need answer with "garbage bags with handles" as example. We can say "Yes! The principle: spend on items you use daily that are cheap but annoying when cheap." Then list.

Need maybe "not all expensive things worth it" but user asks. We can include "avoid spending on brand-name water, etc." But focus.

Let's craft final with categories and bullet points. Need maybe "Here are my favorite upgrades" with 20 items. Keep each one line.

Need ensure not too long. Desired oververbosity 5. We'll do moderate.

Let's write:

- Drawstring trash bags (already)
- Good chef's knife + cutting board
- Quality nonstick pan (replace when scratched)
- Dishwasher detergent pods (Finish)
- Paper towels (select-a-size, strong)
- Toilet paper (not the cheap stuff)
- Tissues with lotion
- Wool socks and good underwear
- Shoes and insoles
- Mattress, pillows, sheets
- Towels
- Ergonomic chair / standing desk
- Large monitor
- Mechanical keyboard / good mouse
- Noise-cancelling headphones
- Phone case and screen protector
- Fast-charging cables and power bank
- Luggage with spinner wheels
- Backpack with padded straps
- Rain jacket / winter coat
- Sunglasses (polarized)
- Sunscreen (nice formula)
- Glass food storage containers
- Heavy-duty aluminum foil / parchment paper
- Robot vacuum / good vacuum
- Air fryer / instant pot
- Burr coffee grinder
- Insulated water bottle
- Windproof umbrella
- Good tires (if car)

Need maybe "The common thread: buy things that are between you and the ground, or that you use every day, at a quality level that doesn't annoy you."

Need maybe "garbage bags with handles" already. Good.

Let's final.

Yes! The principle is: **spend more on things you use every day, or that sit between you and the ground/your hands.** Cheap versions of these cause small daily annoyances; good versions make life noticeably smoother.

Here are my favorite “garbage bag with handles” upgrades:

- **Drawstring trash bags** — you already know.
- **A good chef’s knife** — one solid knife ($80–150) beats a whole cheap block. Keep it sharp.
- **A large wooden or composite cutting board** — doesn’t slide around, doesn’t warp, easier to clean.
- **Quality nonstick pan** — for eggs and delicate stuff. Replace when scratched.
- **Dishwasher detergent pods** — the good ones (Finish Quantum, Cascade Platinum) actually clean better than the bargain bin.
- **Select-a-size paper towels** — stronger, less waste, one sheet handles most messes.
- **Good toilet paper** — 2-ply or better. Life’s too short for sandpaper.
- **Tissues with lotion** — if you get colds, this is a game changer.
- **Wool socks** — Merino or thick wool blends. Warm, breathable, less stinky.
- **Comfortable underwear** — don’t skimp on things that touch your skin all day.
- **Shoes and insoles** — good arch support changes your whole day.
- **Mattress, pillows, and sheets** — you spend a third of your life there. Upgrade sleep.
- **Thick, absorbent towels** — cheap towels feel rough and never fully dry you.
- **An ergonomic office chair** — if you sit at a desk, this is your throne.
- **A large monitor** — less squinting, more screen space, easier on your neck.
- **A mechanical keyboard and a good mouse** — satisfying and comfortable for daily use.
- **Noise-cancelling headphones** — for focus, travel, and sanity.
- **A good phone case and screen protector** — cheaper than a cracked screen.
- **Fast-charging cables and a high-capacity power bank** — Anker or similar. Never wait forever.
- **Luggage with good spinner wheels** — gliding through airports is underrated.
- **A comfortable backpack** — padded straps and good organization make commuting easier.
- **A proper rain jacket** — breathable and waterproof beats a cheap poncho.
- **A warm winter coat** — good insulation is worth every dollar.
- **Polarized sunglasses** — reduce glare, better for driving and being outside.
- **Sunscreen that doesn’t feel gross** — you’ll actually wear it.
- **Glass food storage containers** — no staining, no warping, microwave-safe.
- **Heavy-duty aluminum foil and parchment paper** — no tearing, no sticking.
- **A robot vacuum** — or at least a good vacuum. Floors stay clean with zero effort.
- **An air fryer or Instant Pot** — makes cooking so easy you’ll order less takeout.
- **A burr coffee grinder** — fresh ground coffee tastes dramatically better.
- **An insulated water bottle** — cold water all day, no condensation.
- **A windproof umbrella** — doesn’t flip inside out and die.
- **Good tires** — if you drive, this is the ultimate “between you and the road” upgrade.

The common thread: **buy cheap versions of things you rarely use, but buy good versions of things you use constantly.** That’s the whole secret.
